observations: Red gas cylinder with a metal collar at the top.
The collar has embossed text: 'UKPP 32' and 'PROPERTY OF COMMERCE'.
The main body of the cylinder has a white rectangular label with the text 'CALOR GAS' and '47kg Propellant'.
The cylinder shows significant surface wear and dirt, particularly on the shoulder and body.
A watermark 'POSTED ON JIJI NWOBODO PETER' is visible across the center of the image.

claims.evidence: The capacity is not clearly legible on the visible parts of the cylinder.
This refers to the origin of the cylinder, which cannot be confirmed from a photo.
The manufacturing date is not visible on the cylinder.
The cylinder is red, which is the standard color for LPG in Nigeria, but the specific brand 'Total' is not visible.

risks.risk: The cylinder may be expired or past its re-qualification date.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the manufacturing and expiry date stamps on the collar or handle.

risks.risk: The cylinder may be a counterfeit or a different brand (e.g., Total) than the seller claims.
risks.proof: A photo of the manufacturer's identification plate (usually on the collar) showing the brand and model.

risks.risk: The valve or shroud may be damaged or leaking.
risks.proof: A video showing a soap bubble test on the valve and a close-up of the shroud.
risks.if_unproven: as requiring a full valve replacement

proof_requests: Close-up of any label, sticker or metal plate showing the brand and model.
Photo of the manufacturing and expiry date stamps on the collar.
Photo of the valve and shroud to check for leaks.
Photo of the full cylinder with the collar removed to verify the actual capacity.
response.reason: What the item is shows, but not the model that sets its price: no photo shows it clearly enough to read. The shot asked for first would settle it.
